title: How the Rule of Law Thinks - Toward a Coherent Outcome Test for Medical Negligence
description: This paper critically examines the Bolam Test in English medical negligence law, arguing that it fails to meet the rationality standards required under the rule of law. By deferring legal judgment to unverified professional opinion rather than to defined, reconstructible standards, Bolam undermines legal accountability and patient rights. The paper proposes a structural alternative: the Coherent Outcome Test (COT), which evaluates whether a patient's outcome is logically compatible with the known medical facts and constraints at the time of treatment. Rooted in principles of legal rationality, human dignity, and forward-structured reasoning, COT offers a methodologically sound framework for adjudicating complex clinical decisions under uncertainty. It repositions law as a system designed for intelligent agents—requiring justification, not speculation—and aligns legal oversight with the foundational purpose of medicine: to preserve life and protect the vulnerable.
